sources.entry: Mirumoji - Japanese immersion toolkit providing clickable, tokenized subtitles with dictionary lookups and transcription generation. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: Mirumoji is a self-hosted Japanese immersion toolkit that turns video, anime, drama, or audio into clickable tokenized subtitles with dictionary lookups, whisper-based transcription, clip saving, and Anki export.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a locally run Docker Compose application. Its interactive player loads videos and subtitles and shows clickable, tokenized Japanese lines with dictionary pop-ups. Subtitle generation and audio transcription use faster-whisper, on a local or cloud GPU. Dictionary features include a wildcard search (via kotobase) and a paste-in text analyzer with furigana. Optional LLM integration accepts Gemini, Claude, or GPT API keys, or a local LLM server, to generate sentence breakdowns from customizable prompts. Users can save video segments with word breakdowns and export them as an Anki deck, and keep files organized per profile on the server. A desktop launcher and CLI are provided to run the app, and the README also lists manual setup.
use_cases: study Japanese with anime or drama episodes
look up words while watching Japanese video
create Anki flashcards from video clips
get LLM sentence breakdowns for Japanese text
how_to_run: Download the Desktop Launcher for your platform
Alternatively, set up manually or through the CLI (see the setup guide)
notable: Clickable tokenized Japanese subtitles with instant dictionary pop-ups
Whisper-based subtitle generation on local or cloud GPU (Modal)
Anki deck export of clips with word breakdowns
Optional LLM sentence breakdowns with customizable prompts, including local LLM servers
caveats: Cloud GPU and LLM features are optional and depend on external API keys or a local LLM server
Setup requires Docker and a local Docker Compose environment
README does not describe platform support beyond the Desktop Launcher
